Let $S$ be a scheme. Let $f : X \to Y$ be a morphism of algebraic spaces
over $S$. There exists a closed subspace $Z \subset Y$ such that $f$ factors
through $Z$ and such that for any other closed subspace $Z' \subset Y$
such that $f$ factors through $Z'$ we have $Z \subset Z'$.
hypotheses:

over $S$.
conclusions:
There exists a closed subspace $Z \subset Y$ such that $f$ factors
through $Z$ and such that for any other closed subspace $Z' \subset Y$
such that $f$ factors through $Z'$ we have $Z \subset Z'$.

reason: The universal scheme-theoretic image is the closed subspace cut out by the maximal quasi-coherent ideal inside Ker(O_Y→f_*O_X). Existence of that maximal quasi-coherent subsheaf follows from the previously proved sum construction.

Let $S$ be a scheme.
Let $f : X \to Y$ be a morphism of algebraic spaces over $S$.
Let $Z \subset Y$ be the scheme theoretic image of $f$.
If $f$ is quasi-compact then
\begin{enumerate}
\item the sheaf of ideals
$\mathcal{I} = \Ker(\mathcal{O}_Y \to f_*\mathcal{O}_X)$
is quasi-coherent,
\item the scheme theoretic image $Z$ is the closed subspace
corresponding to $\mathcal{I}$,
\item for any \'etale morphism $V \to Y$ the scheme theoretic image of
$X \times_Y V \to V$ is equal to $Z \times_Y V$, and
\item the image $|f|(|X|) \subset |Z|$ is a dense subset of $|Z|$.
\end{enumerate}

stage_b_reviewed_content.statement:
Scheme-theoretic image is the smallest closed subspace of target through which source map factors.

Let $S$ be a scheme. Let $f : X \to Y$ be a morphism of algebraic spaces
over $S$. Assume $X$ is reduced. Then
\begin{enumerate}
\item the scheme theoretic image $Z$ of $f$ is the reduced induced algebraic
space structure on $\overline{|f|(|X|)}$, and
\item for any \'etale morphism $V \to Y$ the scheme theoretic image of
$X \times_Y V \to V$ is equal to $Z \times_Y V$.
\end{enumerate}
hypotheses:
Let $S$ be a scheme. Let $f : X \to Y$ be a morphism of algebraic spaces
over $S$. Assume $X$ is reduced.

reason: For reduced X, its topological image closure with reduced induced structure is the smallest closed subspace receiving f; étale localizations preserve reducedness and the open étale chart allows the closure to pull back, proving both assertions.

Let $S$ be a scheme.
Let $f : X \to Y$ be a quasi-compact morphism of algebraic spaces over $S$.
Let $Z$ be the scheme theoretic image of $f$.
Let $z \in |Z|$. There exists a valuation ring $A$ with
fraction field $K$ and a commutative diagram
$$
\xymatrix{
\Spec(K) \ar[rr] \ar[d] & & X \ar[d] \ar[ld] \\
\Spec(A) \ar[r] & Z \ar[r] & Y
}
$$
such that the closed point of $\Spec(A)$ maps to $z$.
hypotheses:
Let $S$ be a scheme.
Let $f : X \to Y$ be a quasi-compact morphism of algebraic spaces over $S$.
Let $Z$ be the scheme theoretic image of $f$.
Let $z \in |Z|$.
conclusions:
There exists a valuation ring $A$ with
fraction field $K$ and a commutative diagram
$$
\xymatrix{
\Spec(K) \ar[rr] \ar[d] & & X \ar[d] \ar[ld] \\
\Spec(A) \ar[r] & Z \ar[r] & Y
}
$$
such that the closed point of $\Spec(A)$ maps to $z$.

reason: Take an étale affine scheme chart V→Y through z and replace the pullback X×_YV by a quasi-compact affine étale presentation W. The image of W in V is the same scheme-theoretic image, and the cited scheme valuative lemma produces Spec K→W and Spec A→Z' with closed point mapping to z; composition descends the diagram to X,Y.

Let $S$ be a scheme. Let
$$
\xymatrix{
X_1 \ar[d] \ar[r]_{f_1} & Y_1 \ar[d] \\
X_2 \ar[r]^{f_2} & Y_2
}
$$
be a commutative diagram of algebraic spaces over $S$.
Let $Z_i \subset Y_i$, $i = 1, 2$ be
the scheme theoretic image of $f_i$. Then the morphism
$Y_1 \to Y_2$ induces a morphism $Z_1 \to Z_2$ and a
commutative diagram
$$
\xymatrix{
X_1 \ar[r] \ar[d] & Z_1 \ar[d] \ar[r] & Y_1 \ar[d] \\
X_2 \ar[r] & Z_2 \ar[r] & Y_2
}
$$

Let $Z_i \subset Y_i$, $i = 1, 2$ be

conclusions:
the morphism

reason: The pullback of the scheme-theoretic image Z_2 along Y_1→Y_2 is a closed subspace of Y_1 through which f_1 factors. Minimality of Z_1 thus yields a factorization Z_1→Z_2.

The image Y' is a closed subspace of X, with map Y'→Y induced by f; it becomes isomorphic to Y over V.

Let $S$ be a scheme.
Let $f : X \to Y$ be a separated morphism of algebraic spaces over $S$.
Let $V \subset Y$ be an open subspace such that $V \to Y$ is quasi-compact.
Let $s : V \to X$ be a morphism such that $f \circ s = \text{id}_V$.
Let $Y'$ be the scheme theoretic image of $s$.
Then $Y' \to Y$ is an isomorphism over $V$.
hypotheses:
Let $S$ be a scheme.
Let $f : X \to Y$ be a separated morphism of algebraic spaces over $S$.
Let $V \subset Y$ be an open subspace such that $V \to Y$ is quasi-compact.
Let $s : V \to X$ be a morphism such that $f \circ s = \text{id}_V$.
Let $Y'$ be the scheme theoretic image of $s$.

reason: The section s:V→X is quasi-compact, so its scheme-theoretic image commutes with restriction to the open f^{-1}V. There it coincides with the section of the separated morphism f^{-1}V→V, which is a closed immersion; hence the image is isomorphic to V over V.
